Cheapest tested: €32.93/MWh for two doublets at 3,150 m, CHP and screw-chiller cooling [R0234]. It meets nominal demand but fails heating demand during an unplanned peak outage [R0244].

My provisional recommendation is the version with backup boilers and additional cooling capacity: €34.81/MWh [R0250]. It passes every available stress case [R0251, R0252, R0253, R0254, R0255] and agrees with GEMINI’s Solver at both demand peaks [R0250].

Injector pressure remains assumed equal to producer pressure. The tool cannot vary it, so the cost ranking and performance under that uncertainty remain unver

The cheapest design demonstrated to pass every tested stress case is [R0514]: €33.77/MWh, with €43.54 million capital cost. It uses two 3,100 m doublets, CHP, an ORC, variable-speed pumps, backup gas heating and screw-chiller cooling.

The cheaper nominal design costs €32.34/MWh [R0407], but fails the heating-demand rule during a peak geothermal outage [R0447]. The recommended design passes the tested reservoir, demand, outage, boiler-loss and combined stresses; GEMINI Solver checks also agree [R0565, R0566, R0567, R0489, R0568, R0514].

This is a conditional recommendation: costs assume equal

The cheapest screened design that passes the unplanned peak-outage test is [R0307], at €33.67/MWh: two 3,050 m doublets, CHP using co-produced gas, an electric screw chiller with dry cooling, and gas-boiler backup. Capital cost is €41.79 million. It meets nominal demand, passes the peak-outage test, and agrees with GEMINI’s Solver [R0307, R0314].

The nominal cheapest is €32.57/MWh [R0265], but its peak-outage case leaves 6,527 MWh of heating unmet, breaking the demand rule [R0291].
